title: London’s High Court dissolves The Beatles’ partnership | 1975
content:
Representatives of John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr met at London’s High Court on 9 January 1975 to formally dissolve The Beatles’ business partnership.

A dissolution of contract had been signed by all four former Beatles in late 1974. The private court hearing was to formalise the agreement.

Apple Corps’ business holdings had been under the control of a court-appointed receiver, James Douglas Spooner, since 1971. As of 1 November 1974, it had £8,915.912, of which £2,387,580.99 had been invested at The Beatles’ request.

Relations between the former Beatles were relatively good at the beginning of 1975, a situation which led to a change in direction at Apple. Although the record label and various other side projects were long since abandoned, it was decided that it should continue to oversee joint projects by The Beatles, including their past and any future works, and to distribute royalties accordingly. Under the dissolution agreement any royalties from their solo works would be paid directly to the relevant parties, instead of to Apple.

With the agreement finalised, Apple issued a statement after the High Court hearing:

John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr are happy to announce that all legal and business disputes among them have been settled. All four have signed an agreement enabling each to pursue his own career. At the same time, the former Beatles become directors of Apple Corps Ltd. which will continue to operate from its St. James’s Street offices in London.
Page last updated: 30 December 2025
